hints: Substitute $x = 4y - c$ into $y^2 = x + 3$ to get $y^2 - 4y + (c - 3) = 0$.
Set discriminant $\Delta = (-4)^2 - 4(1)(c - 3) = 0$ for tangency and solve for $c$.
walkthrough:
Rearrange the line equation to express $x$ in terms of $y$:
$$4y = x + c \implies x = 4y - c$$

Substitute into the curve equation $y^2 = x + 3$:
$$y^2 = (4y - c) + 3 \implies y^2 - 4y + (c - 3) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition requiring discriminant $\Delta = 0$:
$$(-4)^2 - 4(1)(c - 3) = 0 \implies 16 - 4c + 12 = 0 \implies 28 - 4c = 0$$
$$4c = 28 \implies c = 7$$

Substitute $c = 7$ into the quadratic equation in $y$:
$$y^2 - 4y + 4 = 0 \implies (y - 2)^2 = 0 \implies y = 2$$

Calculate the corresponding $x$-coordinate using $x = 4y - 7$:
$$x = 4(2) - 7 = 8 - 7 = 1$$
$$\text{Coordinates of } P: \quad (1, 2)$$
